role: the technical writer who maintains generated docs
verdict: No: the spec keeps generated reference true to main's code, but nothing keeps the pages a reader acts on in a failure (fix hints, help, guides, skills) true to the release they run, and after v1.0.0 every docs-currency check stops running.

findings.defect: The checks that keep guides complete and executed (a guide page per journey in tools/ci acceptance; the host suite and block B, which alone run the commands of J1, J3a, J4, J5, J6, J8, J9, J12 and J13) run once, for v1.0.0, and 10 10.5 says a later release does not verify them again.
findings.scenario: v1.2 adds a journey J14 and changes the output of romeu salvage; tools/ci all and release.yml pass; the J14 guide does not exist and the J6 guide shows output no one has seen since the release candidate, while ADR 0001 rule 13 still passes because it only compares command words with commands.yaml.
findings.change: Move the guide-per-journey check from tools/ci acceptance into tools/ci docs (offline, every PR). In 11 11.2 and S7, state that a reduced host-suite run (the journeys outside the CI list) is part of each release, with its result attached to the release, or say plainly in S10 that guides of host-only journeys are unverified after v1.0.0.
findings.cost: A docs-step rule and a test; a release-time maintainer step or an explicit sentence of accepted risk.

findings.defect: The message and the fix hint of every error, and the text of --help, are under no test or check: tests assert ids, never message text (04 4.1), rule 16 is review only, and rule 13 checks commands in README and guides but not the commands a fix hint or help text tells the reader to run.
findings.scenario: A PR renames romeu sync --overwrite-drift; the error table's fix hint for drift still says to run the old flag; every gate passes; the operator at an exit 4 runs the printed command and gets a usage error, or an alias with different behavior.
findings.change: In 04 4.1 add: every command line in the fix column of the error table and in --help examples is matched by the rule 13 matcher against the command definitions, and a fix hint is non-empty and names a command or a page. Add this as a clause of ADR 0001 rule 13 or a new check rule, owned by tools/ci docs or generated.
findings.cost: One matcher reuse and fixtures; a new or amended ADR (ask-first decisions surface).

findings.defect: The docs-versioning row's until-then (the docs on the default branch are the only docs) is itself the defect: a user on release N reads generated errors.md, exit-codes.md and command pages of main, and its trigger is detectable by a check that the row does not name and no one watches after the last review round (ADR 0005 Consequences).
findings.scenario: After v1.0.0 a PR adds an error id and rewrites two fix hints; a v1.0.0 user follows the reference on GitHub for an id their binary prints with a different meaning or hint; the trigger 'first change to a user-facing page after the v1.0.0 tag' fired that week and nothing reported it.
findings.change: Decide before the first tag the minimum: the release attaches the generated reference (docs/reference/*) as a release asset, or links docs at the tag in release notes and README. Make the trigger a check: tools/ci docs (or release.yml) reports a diff of docs/reference, docs/guide or README.md since the last release tag.
findings.cost: A decision (ADR) and one release step or one check.

findings.defect: The guide outline asks for 'recovery from each expected error id' without defining which ids a journey expects, and all thirteen journeys in 09 are success paths, so most error ids, and every failure that is not a journey (drift after a hand edit, an interrupted promotion, julieta setup failing so run does not attach, a blocked host at runtime, RJ-204, ledger-view-writable, an sbx upgrade tripping gate 1), have no recovery page.
findings.scenario: An operator gets exit 4 from romeu run after editing sbxenv.yaml by hand; errors.md gives a one-line hint; no guide covers the case, and the hint's --overwrite-drift silently discards the edit.
findings.change: Add to the error table a column naming the guide section that recovers each id (or 'none: <reason>'); generate errors.md with that link; tools/ci docs fails an id with no section and a section that cites no existing id. Add failure variants to 09 (for example J3c drift, J3d setup failure, J6a incomplete salvage) so the guides that hold them are named by journey id.
findings.cost: A column in the error table, a docs check, three or four journey variants and their scenario functions.

postmortem: Months after v1.0.0 the code works and people stop using it because the docs make failures worse. (1) A user upgrades sbx, gets exit 3 and an id that main's generated errors.md describes differently: docs on main are the only docs and the versioning trigger fired unwatched (index: Deferred decisions; ADR 0001 rule 10; ADR 0005; 04 4.1). (2) Fix hints were the least tested text: ids are asserted, messages never, and rule 13 does not read the commands after 'fix:' (04 4.1; ADR 0001 rules 13 and 16). (3) Every guide was a success path; drift, interrupted promotion, blocked hosts and exit 5 with over-cap had no page, and doctor's checks had no ids (09; 12 12.8; 04 4.2; 08 8.5). (4) Guides were written after the only real-host run and never run again; expected output was typed, not observed (12 12.2; 11 11.2; 10 10.1, 10 10.5; ADR 0001 rule 13). (5) The agent's skills lagged the live julieta binary until recreate (06 6.3, 06 6.4; 08 8.1). (6) The spec taught caveat-instead-of-delete: 05 5.4, 10 10.2, 12 12.4, 12 12.9 kept a review requirement that was gone, ADR 0003 stated it plainly, ADR 0008 chose not to rewrite (ADR 0001 rule 3). (7) Two copies of every format table survived, and readers trusted the better-written stale one (03; 01 1.4; 12 12.3). (8) Unsaid: we spent the docs budget on how ADR numbers are linked and on PR-body prose, and none on telling a frightened person what is safe to run next; the plan's own hand-kept counts were wrong within days and we let it pass (ADR 0001 rules 9 and 18; plan.md). (9) Release notes were a commit log with no upgrade section (12 12.6; J9).
lens_critique: This lens equates success with documentation that is current and recoverable, but for this product the strongest recovery path is the binary itself: deterministic preflight, exit codes, salvage that refuses to destroy, and status as a projection of state. A writer's lens over-weights pages and under-weights making the CLI self-explaining (status and doctor printing the next command, offline explain), which needs no versioned site at all. It also treats every stale sentence as a defect, while for a one-maintainer project some history in current-state text is cheaper than the machinery that would remove it.
missing_viewpoint: No lens is the first-time reader who never opens the spec: an evaluator who meets only the README, the release page and the first error, judging whether to install and whether to trust the tool with their host and credentials (L10 adopts it; nobody judges the decision to adopt).

out_of_scope.why: the text alone cannot settle it: no error table, fix hint or guide exists at baseline; a usability run of the J6 and J10 guides with a real failure would

out_of_scope.what: rule 18 scores and the voice of the spec pages
out_of_scope.why: the text alone cannot settle it: the rubric is a review judgment and no report exists; a scored review per page would

out_of_scope.what: the correctness of security, ledger and gate mechanics
out_of_scope.why: this person would not look at it beyond how it is documented; L2, L13 and L16 judge it

out_of_scope.what: GitHub Pages or any docs hosting choice
out_of_scope.why: this person would defer it; the spec names no site and the versioning decision comes first

confidence: High on the structural gaps (each cited sentence was read, the rule 9 and citation scans were run over the export); medium on severities, which depend on how much of the gap the plan will close.
